 Predicted line-ups for Premier League teams in Matchweek 9
 Ben Bloom
 30 Oct 2026
 See which players we think will start for their clubs this weekend
 Football writer Ben Bloom is predicting how every Premier League team will line up in the remaining fixtures of Matchweek 9.
 Click on the following links to jump to the relevant match
 LIVARS | NEWEVE 
 See:  Injury updates for every club and player 
 See: Who's suspended or close to a ban? 
 Liverpool v Arsenal predicted line-ups 
 Liverpool: Head coach Andoni Iraola confirmed Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz both “have a chance” of making this game after missing the last two, although there does not appear to be a great need to risk them. The same XI that won Liverpool’s last Premier League match remain available and may well be called upon again.
 Arsenal: There are plenty of unknowns for Arsenal, with manager Mikel Arteta saying “we do not know yet” if Noni Madueke will be able to play, while Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori and Christos Tzolis are training and should be available “if everything is ok”. Madueke’s potential absence would be a headache given Max Dowman is suspended. Kai Havertz could be reinstated for Viktor Gyokeres, and Ben White versus Jurrien Timber is a toss up.
 Back to top 
 Newcastle v Everton predicted line-ups 
 Newcastle: After defeat against the same opposition on Thursday, it will be interesting to see how much head coach Matthias Jaissle changes here. Joelinton will come back in after a rest, while Anthony Elanga played a half and must now be pushing for a start. William Osula seems highly unlikely to play after suffering an ankle injury, which could see Yoane Wissa lead the line, with Matias Fernandez-Pardo absent of late. Lewis Miley has also missed the last two games.
 Everton: Jack Grealish was omitted from Thursday’s EFL Cup match due to a “breach of club discipline” and manager David Moyes refused to confirm his availability for this. Everton triumphed without him and it looks like Brennan Johnson, Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling will fight for the two wing spots. Jarrad Branthwaite “should have recovered” after missing the last two games due to concussion protocols. Jake O’Brien can deputise if required. Hayden Hackney will challenge Harrison Armstrong’s place.
